newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks end at record despite BHP slide.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks end at record despite BHP slide.

text.p: SPI Sycom cl 2582.0 +24.0 US 30yr 6.99 steady
10yrbond futs 92.375 -0.045 Gold NY 344.40 Lon fix 341.65
*Stocks ended at a record closing high despite a sharp fall in the shares of bellwether, BHP. Volume 334.5 million, value A$731.4 million, 1,123 stocks traded, 358 steady, 484 up, 281 down.

The Australia share market ended with its fourth straight record close on Monday, climbing solidly in response to a Dow jump on Friday and ignoring the fall of its biggest company, Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd.
The All Ordinaries Index finished up 20.9 points at 2,584.8 which was also its intra-day high and its all-time record high, eclipsing Friday's record mark of 2,572.7 by 12.1 points.
The June contract of the share price index ended up 24 points at 2582, a 2.8 point discount to the physical index.
Turnover at A$735 million was modest in comparison to recent sessions when the market has traded in excess of A$1 billion.
BHP stock sagged after the company said it expected a flat performance until it restructured its operations.
Dealers said the market could have finished 10 points high if BHP had remained steady and up to 20 points firmer if it had pushed ahead with the market.
"There was good broad support for the market which built up as the day went along," said Jamie Spiteri, a dealer at Sydney firm, Shaw Stockbroking.
Spiteri said he expected the market to have a steady to better session on Tuesday as investors stayed on the sidelines due to holiday closures of New York and London equity markets.
Dealers said BHP's fall did, however, benefit its resource peers, as investors were seen switching into CRA Ltd and WMC Ltd stock.
CRA ended up 26.5 cents at A$21.915 and WMC up 20 cents at A$8.48. BHP ended 40 cents weaker at A$18.92 and touched an intra-day low of A$18.75.

Brokers said a 0.5 percentage point rate cut announced on Friday also continued to affect the market with switching seen continuing to occur out of growth stocks into cyclical stocks, such as the retail and building materials and construction related stocks.

Amongst the strongest performers on the day was retailer Woolworths Ltd, whose shares ended up 17 cents at A$4.14 and building materials and sugar refiner, CSR Ltd which closed 14 cents higher at A$4.69.
Australia and New Zealand Banking Group was the strongest of the four major banks ahead of its half year results release on Wednesday. ANZ shares closed up 21.5 cents at A$8.53.

Pharmaceutical group F.H. Faulding & Co was among the few weaker issues on the day as investors factored in possible negative effects on earnings caused by changes made by the government to the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme.
In other markets, long-dated Australian bond yields rose slightly as the market drew breath after Friday's post-rate cut rally, meandering in a narrow range for most of the day.
The yield on 10 year T-bonds closed at 7.61 percent, up 0.04 percentage points compared to Friday's close.

The Australian dollar staged a late recovery from a move towards support, but remained within sight of its 1997 lows as eroded interest rate differentials and a strengthening German mark weighed on the unit, traders said.
By 5.30 p.m. (0730 GMT), the Australian dollar was trading at U$0.7660/65, after opening at US$0.7663/68.
